title: Noisy Label Removal for Partial Multi-Label Learning

problem.claim: Partial multi-label learning assigns each sample a candidate label set containing both ground-truth and noisy labels.

gap.claim: Accurately removing noisy labels is identified as the key unresolved challenge because candidate-label supervision is unreliable.

contributions.claim: A constrained regression model is proposed to learn a PML classifier and select noisy labels, with constraints enforcing their location and binary value.
A competitive classifier based on non-candidate labels is constructed to support noisy-label selection, with mutual learning between the two classifiers.
The model is formulated as a discrete optimization problem and solved using an alternative algorithm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on 6 real-world and 7 synthetic partial multi-label data sets reportedly show significant outperformance over state-of-the-art PML methods across various evaluation metrics.
The authors report that the code implementation is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames partial multi-label learning as weakly supervised learning with candidate sets containing true and noisy labels.
More noisy labels enlarge the generalization error bound and degrade classification performance, making noisy-label removal central.
The approach uses prior knowledge about noisy-label location and values in a constrained regression model.
A classifier built from non-candidate labels competes with the PML classifier and encourages mutual learning.
The discrete optimization model is solved by an alternative algorithm and evaluated on real-world and synthetic data sets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the generalization bound or its assumptions.
